newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel declined slightly on Wednesday against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies in mixed trading, dealers said.
"Trading was mixed and trendless and the dollar closed almost unchanged," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
"Investors are sitting on the fence waiting to see what will happen with the planned budget cut. Investors do not believe the government will approve further cuts without raising taxes," he added.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the Treasury would propose an additional two billion shekels in 1997 budget cuts by early December.

The additional spending reductions will come on top of 4.9 billion shekels the government has already submitted to parliament. The supplementary cuts will now be incorporated into the original budget package.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2320 shekels against 3.2310 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6490 shekels against 3.6439 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9084 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8989 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1561 shekels against 2.1497 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2320 shekels.
